value: exudate output rose with increasing CO2 concentration, dosage-dependent (p<0.0001, n=12-20, two-way ANOVA)
method: behavioural: exudate assay, mass of exudate excreted by a worm exposed to CO2-air mixtures
conditions: Single worms were placed one at a time in a glass petri dish with filter paper and the dish was saturated with air containing a set percentage of CO2 (about 32 ml/s flow) for one minute; the response is exudate excreted, a noxious-stimulus readout, not a measure of detection threshold; control was room air (0% CO2); doses 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100% CO2; n = 12 to 20 worms per analysis; the Discussion says 25% CO2 produced no significant response, so the dose-dependence is carried by higher doses; Methods and legend say one-way ANOVA while the Results text says two-way; worms rinsed in distilled water before testing gave more exudate (n = 6 to 12); worm source, age and health screening not given in the passages read

source.authors: Smith EJ, Ryan JL, Lopresti SA, Haghnazari DBS, Anderson KAS, Lipson SJ, Johnson EC, Silver WL, Saunders CJ
source.title: Mechanisms of carbon dioxide detection in the earthworm Dendrobaena veneta

quote: Earthworms excreted more exudate with increasing concentrations of CO2 in a dosage-dependent manner (p<0.0001, n=12-20, two-way ANOVA) …
note: Quote cut after the statistics; the rest of the sentence lists the concentrations tested. CO2 response is skin-surface chemoreception of a noxious gas; the paper reports transcripts for carbonic anhydrase, ASIC, TRPA1 and OTOP genes but no ionotropic gustatory receptors.

value: the carbonic anhydrase inhibitor acetazolamide significantly muted the exudate response to CO2 (p<0.01, n=8-13)
method: pharmacology: blocker applied before the CO2 exudate assay
conditions: Acetazolamide 50 mM with water as vehicle control (concentration and vehicle from the Results text read, not from the quoted sentence); other carbonic anhydrase blockers: indisulam 0.01 mM also reduced the response (p<0.05, n=6-8) but U-104, S4 and topiramate at 0.01 mM did not (p>0.05, n=6-8); guanylate cyclase (methylene blue), TRPA1 (HC030013) and OTOP1 (ZnCl2) blockers had no effect (p>0.05); acetazolamide did not change the response to the irritant AITC (n=4), so the effect is specific to the CO2 response; same CO2 assay as the dose-response record

source.authors: Smith EJ, Ryan JL, Lopresti SA, Haghnazari DBS, Anderson KAS, Lipson SJ, Johnson EC, Silver WL, Saunders CJ
source.title: Mechanisms of carbon dioxide detection in the earthworm Dendrobaena veneta

quote: The broad-spectrum CA inhibitor acetazolamide significantly muted the response to CO2 (Figure 7A, p<0.01, n=8-13).
note: Pharmacological evidence for carbonic anhydrase in CO2 detection; no receptor cell was recorded.

value: response to brown snake scent differed significantly from the water control (P = 0.005) and the novel control (P = 0.022)
method: behavioural: tongue flicks at scented paper towels in the enclosure, PERMANOVA pair-wise tests
conditions: 57 pygmy bluetongue lizards in three groups: 20 wild (Burra), 9 wild-born captive adults (Monarto Safari Park) and 28 captive-born predator-naive young; each lizard met each scent on a separate day over five days in random order; scent = dampened paper towel left 48 h in a reptile enclosure, frozen at -20 C and used within 3 weeks, placed in the lizard's enclosure; 30 min acclimation then 30 min filmed, tongue flicks at the scent paper counted; eastern brown snake scent came from one animal, the other reptile scents were probably pooled; scents were eastern brown snake, eastern bluetongue lizard, Rosenberg's monitor, a novel control (diluted eucalyptus oil) and a water control; the Results say there was no significant difference among the other treatments, tongue flicks did not differ significantly among lizard origins or days, and lizards basked for a similar time with all scents; no scent dose is given; no health screening is reported; temperature 16.8 to 30.1 C used as a covariate

source.authors: Daniell TL, Hutchinson MN, Ainsley P, Gardner MG
source.title: Recognition of reptile predator scent is innate in an endangered lizard species

where: Results, Differential response to scent treatments
quote: Response to the brown snake treatment differed significantly from both the water control (PERMANOVA pair-wise test P = 0.005) and novel control (PERMANOVA pair-wise test P = 0.022).
note: The sentence says response; the response counted was tongue flicks. Authors read the result as innate recognition of a predator by scent. Licence on the CSIRO page is CC BY-NC.

value: significant between-group main effect for larvae distribution with a bullfrog visible versus no bullfrog (GEE beta = 0.164, p = 0.011)
method: behavioural: spatial distribution of larvae (generalized estimating equation model) with a visible predator behind a clear panel
conditions: Larvae hatched in the lab from eggs collected in April-May 2024 and reared without predator exposure; larval age not stated; 30 replicates of 5 larvae per group; 60 x 30 x 10 cm acrylic tank, water 4.5 cm deep, three compartments separated by clear acrylic panels; one American bullfrog (about 258 g in the large class) placed randomly in a side compartment, control had empty side compartments with water at the same depth; 5 min acclimation then larvae counted at 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 min; chemical cues excluded by a 48 h leak check of the dividers; the group-by-time interaction is reported significant from 4 min and the text and Table 2 give different p values for the 4 min interaction (0.018 versus 0.004)

source.authors: Feng S, Li W, An D, Ma Z, Luo Z, Xu A
source.title: Avoidance Behavior in Chinhai Spiny Newt Larvae: Responses to Visual and Chemical Cues from a Novel Predator

quote: Based on the results of the Generalized Estimating Equation (GEE) model (Table 2), the between-group main effect was significant (β = 0.164, Wald χ2 = 6.416, p = 0.011).
note: Larvae of an endangered newt responded to a bullfrog it has not co-evolved with. The sentence states the effect size; the paper's wording is that visual cues alone produced quick avoidance and lower activity.

value: larval midline crossings with bullfrog odour water 3.167 +/- 1.555, significantly lower than control 5.500 +/- 2.240
method: behavioural: midline crossings in 10 min after injecting bullfrog-conditioned water into a side compartment
conditions: Chemical cue = 30 mL of water conditioned 24 h by four adult bullfrogs fed frog tadpoles (1 L sun-exposed water, filtered), injected into one side compartment through 2 mm perforated partitions; control 30 mL plain sun-exposed water; 30 replicates of 5 larvae per group; larvae lab-hatched, predator-naive, age not stated; odour concentration not given beyond the volume; the same chemical cue produced no significant overall spatial avoidance (see the companion record)

source.authors: Feng S, Li W, An D, Ma Z, Luo Z, Xu A
source.title: Avoidance Behavior in Chinhai Spiny Newt Larvae: Responses to Visual and Chemical Cues from a Novel Predator

quote: In the experimental group, the total number of midline crossings by larvae within 10 min was 3.167 ± 1.555 times, which was significantly lower than that in the control group (5.500 ± 2.240 times).
note: Activity reduction to a chemical cue; no avoidance was found.

value: no significant main effect of group on larval spatial distribution with bullfrog odour water (GEE beta = 0.188, p = 0.205)
method: behavioural: spatial distribution of larvae (generalized estimating equation model) after bullfrog-conditioned water was added to one side compartment
conditions: Null result for avoidance by odour alone; the group-by-time interaction was significant only at 6 min (beta = -0.302, p = 0.042); 30 replicates of 5 larvae per group; chemical cue = 30 mL of water conditioned 24 h by four adult bullfrogs, control 30 mL plain water; bullfrog odour dose beyond volume not given; larvae lab-hatched and predator-naive; the same cue lowered activity (see the companion record)

source.authors: Feng S, Li W, An D, Ma Z, Luo Z, Xu A
source.title: Avoidance Behavior in Chinhai Spiny Newt Larvae: Responses to Visual and Chemical Cues from a Novel Predator

quote: Based on the results of the Generalized Estimating Equation model (Table 4), the main effect of group was not significant (β = 0.188, Wald χ2 = 1.608, p = 0.205).
